nodes.label: search[UCT]
nodes.observation: UCT: UCT is the selection rule most Monte Carlo Tree Search implementations use. Kocsis and Szepesvari derived it from the UCB1 bandit algorithm and presented it at ECML in 2006.

nodes.label: search[Monte Carlo Tree Search]
nodes.observation: Monte Carlo Tree Search: Monte Carlo Tree Search is a planning algorithm that grows a tree of simulated futures. Remi Coulom introduced it, presenting Efficient Selectivity and Backup Operators for Monte-Carlo Tree Search at Computers and Games in 2006.

nodes.label: search[Reflexion]
nodes.observation: Reflexion: Reflexion turns a failed attempt into a written note that is placed in the next prompt. Shinn and colleagues presented it at NeurIPS in 2023. It reflects, but it does not search.

nodes.label: search[Monte Carlo Tree Search]
nodes.observation: Monte Carlo Tree Search: Monte Carlo Tree Search is a planning algorithm that grows a tree of simulated futures. Remi Coulom introduced it, presenting Efficient Selectivity and Backup Operators for Monte-Carlo Tree Search at Computers and Games in 2006.

nodes.label: search[Reasoning via Planning]
nodes.observation: Reasoning via Planning: Reasoning via Planning, or RAP, runs Monte Carlo Tree Search using the language model itself as the world model. Hao and colleagues presented it at EMNLP in 2023.

nodes.label: search[AlphaGo]
nodes.observation: AlphaGo: AlphaGo paired Monte Carlo Tree Search with a policy network and a value network. Silver and colleagues published it in Nature in 2016.

nodes.label: search[Language Agent Tree Search]
nodes.observation: Language Agent Tree Search: Language Agent Tree Search, or LATS, was presented at ICML in 2024 by Zhou, Yan, Shlapentokh-Rothman, Wang and Wang. It adapts Monte Carlo Tree Search to language agents, adding a language model value function, real environment feedback, and a reflection step.
